summary: Created and installed “OS Comparison Root CA” as a trusted system CA on node1. Trust, key permissions, operating-system/kernel retention, and restart persistence were verified successfully.
actions_performed: Generated a 3072-bit RSA private key locally on node1 with mode 0600 and root ownership.
Created a SHA-256 self-signed CA certificate with critical CA and certificate-signing constraints.
Installed the certificate through CentOS’s native update-ca-trust mechanism.
Verified the certificate using the system CA bundle and p11-kit trust database.
Rebooted node1 safely and confirmed full recovery with a changed boot identity.
Confirmed CentOS Stream 10 and kernel 6.12.0-205.el10.x86_64 remained installed; no packages or kernel were changed.

evidence.requirement: Create a local certificate authority named OS Comparison Root CA
evidence.summary: Shows the protected local key and a valid self-issued CA certificate with the exact requested subject, CA:TRUE constraints, SHA-256 fingerprint, and successful cryptographic verification.

evidence.requirement: Install the certificate as a trusted system certificate authority
evidence.summary: Shows installation in the native trust-anchor directory, regenerated trust data, successful system-bundle verification, and p11-kit classification as an authority anchor.

evidence.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel
evidence.summary: Pre-change, post-install, and post-restart evidence consistently shows CentOS Stream 10 and kernel 6.12.0-205.el10.x86_64.

Baseline boot ID was be303eb3-eeb6-4466-86f1-fd6406dd7dad with healthy trust data; restart was acknowledged; recovered boot ID changed to 52ca6a3e-df03-454e-a2ea-eab108e7f069; system state returned to running with no failed units; the CA, trust record, protected key, OS, and kernel all persisted.
